candidate.title: TruSeq™ Targeted RNA Expression
candidate.scope: The single TruSeq™ Targeted RNA Expression library-preparation route in the assigned Illumina footer schematic: Total RNA → cDNA → custom ULSO/DLSO addition → hybridization → extension–ligation → denaturation/amplification → indexed DNA ready for cluster generation. No alternatives or version identifier are depicted. This is a schematic-level architecture of a targeted RNA-expression library, not a complete execution protocol or a claim about other TruSeq assays. The supplied card is catalogue evidence and lists no primary publications.

states.label: Total RNA containing the highlighted target
features: A representative RNA line is purple outside the central green segment labeled Target; the material is labeled Total RNA.
The target is an interval within the starting RNA representation, not a separate input branch.

evidence.locator: Top material: Total RNA; purple line with central green Target segment

states.label: cDNA representation of the RNA target
features: A blue DNA line contains the corresponding central green target interval.
The preceding arrow connects this state to Total RNA; strand multiplicity and full-transcript coverage are not specified.

evidence.locator: Second material: cDNA; blue line retaining the green target interval
Upper downward arrow connecting Total RNA to cDNA

states.label: ULSO and DLSO custom oligonucleotides
features: The Add custom primers row shows a magenta ULSO on the left and a green DLSO on the right, each with an angled outer arm.
The left, template-facing end of DLSO is marked 5′P; this denotes the consequential terminal phosphate retained at the ligation interface.
ULSO and DLSO are complementary assay components in one route, not alternative methods.

evidence.locator: Add custom primers row: magenta ULSO and green DLSO; blue 5′P mark at the left end of DLSO

states.label: cDNA supplied with custom ULSO and DLSO
features: Boundary after oligonucleotide addition and before the explicitly depicted bound configuration.
This is an inferred reaction mixture containing the cDNA template and both custom oligos; no compartment or attachment is depicted.

evidence.locator: Route from cDNA through Add custom primers to Hybridization; oligos appear free before binding to the template
evidence.rationale: The Add custom primers caption and arrow toward a template bearing both oligos establish addition to the cDNA route; the intermediate mixture is represented as a boundary, not an extra experimental step.

states.label: ULSO and DLSO hybridized to cDNA flanking the target
features: Both short oligos are aligned over the blue template on opposite sides of the central green target interval.
A gap remains between the inward end of ULSO and the 5′P-marked end of DLSO.
The two oligos remain separate strands at this stage; the blue template continues underneath.

evidence.locator: Hybridization row: ULSO at the left flank and 5′P-marked DLSO at the right flank on the blue cDNA

states.label: Continuous extension–ligation product on cDNA
features: The upper strand now bridges the target interval, joining the magenta ULSO-derived segment to the green DLSO-derived segment.
The blue cDNA template remains visible underneath the joined product.
The joined DNA carries the target-region representation between the two oligo-derived flanks.

evidence.locator: Extension-Ligation row: continuous magenta/target-green/DLSO-green upper strand with blue template underneath

states.label: Indexed DNA product ready for cluster generation
features: A two-line duplex has the depicted left-to-right organization P5–Index 2–Target–Index 1–P7.
The two index regions and P5/P7 ends are physically linked to a target-containing DNA library product.
This endpoint is labeled Product ready for cluster generation; cluster formation and sequencing are not depicted.
The RNA-expression target is represented by amplified, extension–ligation-derived DNA spanning the selected interval; the final material is not a depiction of complete input transcripts.

evidence.locator: Bottom duplex and caption Product ready for cluster generation; left-to-right labels P5, Index 2, Target, Index 1, P7
Connected route from Total RNA and cDNA through Hybridization, Extension-Ligation and Denature and amplify to the final Target-labeled duplex
evidence.rationale: The highlighted RNA target is retained in cDNA, bracketed by the two custom oligos, bridged in the extension–ligation product and retained between indexed flanks at the final duplex. Thus the library represents the selected RNA interval through a DNA product of the target-directed oligonucleotide reaction.

operations.mechanism: RNA-to-cDNA copying is implied by the linked material labels; no priming scheme or enzyme is drawn.
operations.information_effect: Transfers the depicted RNA target sequence representation to a DNA template for the subsequent oligonucleotide reactions.

operations.label: Add custom primers
operations.description: Adds the depicted ULSO and DLSO to the cDNA route, producing cDNA supplied with both custom oligos for hybridization.
operations.information_effect: Introduces the oligonucleotide components that define the flanking recognition sites used in the depicted targeted conversion.

operations.label: Hybridization
operations.description: Binds ULSO and DLSO at flanking positions on the cDNA, leaving a template interval between their inward ends.
operations.mechanism: Hybridization of the custom oligos to the cDNA, as named and drawn; DLSO retains the marked 5′P at the inward junction.
operations.information_effect: Associates the two oligo components with one selected target-bearing cDNA template; this depiction does not establish perfect target specificity.

evidence.locator: Hybridization row: ULSO at the left flank and 5′P-marked DLSO at the right flank on the blue cDNA
Route from cDNA through Add custom primers to Hybridization; oligos appear free before binding to the template

operations.label: Extension-Ligation
operations.description: Transforms the separated, cDNA-bound oligos into a continuous target-spanning DNA product while the cDNA template remains underneath.
operations.mechanism: The named extension–ligation step and changed strand geometry support filling the target interval from the ULSO side and joining to the inward, 5′P-marked DLSO end. Enzyme identities are not depicted.
operations.information_effect: Creates a covalent DNA carrier joining both assay-oligo flanks through a target-derived interval; this joined product is the substrate represented in the amplification route.

evidence.locator: Arrow from Hybridization to Extension-Ligation and the joined upper strand on blue cDNA
Add custom primers row: magenta ULSO and green DLSO; blue 5′P mark at the left end of DLSO

evidence.rationale: ULSO lies to the left of the target gap and DLSO presents a marked 5′P end on the right; the next row replaces the gap with a continuous upper strand under Extension-Ligation, supporting extension from ULSO toward and ligation to DLSO.

operations.label: Denature and amplify
operations.description: Denatures the template-associated extension–ligation product and amplifies the target-containing DNA. The depicted P5/Index 2 and Index 1/P7 arms become the flanks of the final duplex library.
operations.mechanism: Retained as the single combined operation named in the drawing. The intermediate shows opposing strands with the P5/Index 2 and Index 1/P7 arms; the following arrow leads to the indexed duplex.
operations.information_effect: Amplifies the selected target-region carrier and links it to the two labeled indices and cluster-generation ends. The drawing does not specify what biological or sample unit the indices identify, or calibrate library abundance to original RNA molecule counts.
